title: Junta Gyrocopters and Mi-35 Helicopter Kill Seven Civilians in Sagaing's Ye-U Township
detail: At around 4:48 p.m. on September 7, 2026, three gyrocopters and one Mi-35 attack helicopter launched from the Northwestern Regional Military Command in Monywa struck a vehicle repair workshop near the market in Tinteinyan Village, Ye-U Township, Sagaing Region. The aircraft dropped bombs and opened fire with machine guns, killing a woman and six men aged 20-50 instantly and wounding three others. The workshop, neighboring market stalls, and at least 10 vehicles were destroyed or badly damaged. Residents and resistance officials said there was no active fighting in the area at the time of the strike.

media.caption: Aftermath of the September 7 junta gyrocopter and Mi-35 helicopter attack on a vehicle repair workshop in Tinteinyan Village, Ye-U Township.

title: Junta Jet Bombs Thandwe's Ward No. 8, Killing Elderly Woman
detail: A junta fighter jet struck Ward No. 8 of Thandwe town, Rakhine State, at around 10:30 a.m. on September 7, 2026, dropping two 300-pound bombs and strafing the area with machine-gun fire. An elderly woman was killed and three civilians were seriously injured; six homes were damaged. The strike came as junta air and naval forces continued bombarding Thandwe and Gwa townships, with warships shelling Gwa, Kyeintali and Gyeik Taw areas from offshore positions since September 3.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the September 7 junta airstrike on Thandwe's Ward No. 8.

title: NUG Marks Fifth Anniversary of 'People's Defensive War', Awards Honors to 1,792 Resistance Members
detail: The National Unity Government held a ceremony at 10:00 a.m. on September 7, 2026 marking the fifth anniversary of its declaration of the 'People's Defensive War' and the establishment of the People's Defence Force. More than 300 people attended, including NUG Acting President Duwa Lashi La and Prime Minister Mahn Win Khaing Than, along with CRPH/NUCC representatives, federal-unit governments, allied resistance organizations, and PDF/PDO commanders and fighters. The NUG presented military honors, medals and decorations to 1,792 resistance members across five categories, including one Hero of the People's Revolution award, 21 People's Revolution Hero awards, 1,647 People's Martyr awards, 81 People's Good Son awards and 42 Revolutionary Service medals.
